claims.text: A machine-learning-augmented ab initio phonon-transport approach can identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will be more accurate and reliable than conventional phonon-gas or simplified ab initio methods.
The targeted high-entropy alloys have high configurational disorder.
The targeted high-entropy alloys exhibit complex lattice distortions.
Disorder descriptors can be extracted from detailed atomic-scale configurations and used in phonon-transport prediction.
The proposed workflow integrates a machine-learning model with ab initio phonon-transport simulations.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can provide experimental measurements suitable for validating the predicted thermal conductivity.
The approach is expected to apply from room temperature to elevated temperatures when phonons are the primary heat carriers.
Configurational disorder has nonlinear effects on phonon scattering.
Lattice distortions have nonlinear effects on phonon scattering.
Atomic-configuration-derived disorder descriptors capture the complex relationship between lattice imperfections and phonon scattering.
Using disorder descriptors as machine-learning features improves phonon thermal-conductivity prediction relative to models that neglect the full effects of chemical disorder.
The proposed predictions will correlate with experimental thermal-conductivity measurements.
The proposed predictions will have lower error than predictions from traditional models.
Simplified phonon-gas and standard ab initio models inadequately capture severe lattice distortions and configurational disorder.
Improved prediction requires sufficient atomic-scale data that accurately represent the alloy disorder.
The approach may not apply when strong electron-phonon coupling or magnetic fluctuations dominate thermal transport.
The approach may not generalize when the training dataset does not encompass the complexity of the tested alloy compositions.
The magnitude of prediction-error reduction may vary among alloy systems and temperature ranges.
Predictive performance depends on the quality of the disorder descriptors and the representativeness of the training dataset.
